established_findings.statement: LLMs are actively applied to intent-driven network management and intent→configuration translation, with prototypes, benchmarks, and at least one production-framed framework reported.
established_findings.evidence_type: empirical and system papers / framework reports
limitations: Scope and maturity vary by work (from prototype/testbed to claimed production); independent cross-vendor, large-scale validation is limited in these records.

established_findings.statement: Tool-augmented architectures (LLMs invoking external tools, RAG, multi-tool agents) are a common pattern proposed and evaluated to improve grounding, factuality, and task automation in domain workflows relevant to NetOps.
established_findings.evidence_type: system papers, focused studies, and surveys
limitations: Many demonstrations are cross-domain (statistics, chemistry, drilling) or survey-level; direct NetOps-only empirical head-to-head comparisons are fewer in the supplied records.

established_findings.statement: There is substantial literature documenting hallucination and constraint-violation failures in LLM outputs and proposing detection/mitigation techniques (e.g., entropy-based detectors, constrained decoding, self-consistency/verification).
limitations: Mitigation methods reduce but do not eliminate failures; many evaluations target general-language or non-NetOps benchmarks rather than large-scale operational NetOps deployments.

established_findings.statement: Architectural guardrails—protocol-mediated execution, runtime authorization (twin/verification), and execution-witness or proof-carrying authorization—are proposed as necessary governance layers for agentic systems that act on infrastructure.
established_findings.evidence_type: architectural and prototype defense papers / surveys
limitations: Prototypes show efficacy under modeled conditions; robustness under real-world sensor/state mismatch and adversarial adaptation varies across studies.

established_findings.statement: Benchmarks and evaluation suites for LLMs in networking/security contexts exist (e.g., NetConfEval, CyberMetric, AIOpsArena, LLM honeypot benchmarks), but cover different tasks and axes.
limitations: Existing benchmarks focus on disparate subtasks (QA, configuration translation, microservice AIOps, honeypot realism) and no single unified safety/verification NetOps benchmark is evident in these records.

unresolved_questions.statement: How reliably do LLM-driven intent→configuration pipelines produce operationally safe, deployment-grade network changes across diverse vendors and real production states?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: mixed (prototype reports and surveys highlighting limited external validation)
limitations: Some frameworks report production use (e.g., Confucius) but independent, quantified, cross-vendor failure-rate reporting is limited in the supplied records.

unresolved_questions.statement: Can verifier/authorization layers (digital twins, protocol-mediated governance) maintain safety under realistic measurement noise, state mismatch, and adversarial or indirect prompt-injection in NetOps settings?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: prototype evaluation papers and security attack study
limitations: Some papers evaluate model-mismatch scenarios; full-spectrum adversarial robustness evaluations specific to NetOps remain sparse in these records.

unresolved_questions.statement: Is there a consensus metric suite that jointly captures functional correctness, safety (policy compliance), and risk (blast radius) for generated network changes?
limitations: Multiple proposals exist but no single, widely-adopted integrated metric suite appears in the supplied records.

unresolved_questions.statement: Which is more effective for preventing harmful NetOps actions on configuration synthesis tasks: constrained-decoding (hard-constraint generation) or external verify-and-repair workflows?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: method papers and surveys indicating methodological alternatives
limitations: Constrained-decoding methods and verify/repair are evaluated mainly outside NetOps in these records; direct head-to-head NetOps comparisons are not present among the supplied records.

candidate_gaps.statement: A unified, safety-focused NetOps benchmark that evaluates end-to-end generate→verify→authorize→apply pipelines (including measurement noise, vendor heterogeneity, and adversarial data injections) is not evident in the supplied records.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: gap inference from benchmark and survey literature
limitations: Existing benchmarks cover portions of the pipeline; this absence claim is limited to the supplied record set.

candidate_gaps.statement: Systematic empirical studies that quantify real-world failure modes (frequency, root causes, operational impact) of LLM-generated network configurations under production-like perturbations are scarce in the supplied records.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: inference from prototypes and surveys lacking extensive failure-data
limitations: Some authors report operational experience but systematic, quantified failure-mode datasets are not prominent in these records.

candidate_gaps.statement: Standardized evaluation metrics that integrate security threat models (indirect prompt injection, malicious tool use) with NetOps correctness metrics are underdeveloped in the supplied literature.
limitations: Security taxonomies and threat mappings exist, but their formal integration with operational NetOps correctness benchmarks is not evident among the supplied records.

candidate_gaps.statement: Direct comparative evaluations of constrained-decoding (hard-constraint generation) versus external verifier-first architectures specifically on network-configuration synthesis tasks are missing from the supplied records.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: method papers and surveys indicating methodological divergence
limitations: Constrained-decoding research is present but primarily assessed outside NetOps; direct comparative NetOps studies are not supplied.

excluded_claims: LLMs are ready to operate unguarded as autonomous NetOps agents in production without external verification or governance (no supplied record provides unqualified empirical support).
Any single architectural pattern (e.g., tool-augmented agents) universally eliminates hallucination or unsafe outputs across NetOps (unsupported by supplied empirical evidence).
There is conclusive evidence that constrained decoding alone guarantees production-grade safety for network configuration generation (no NetOps-specific proof in the supplied records).
